title: Detailed ridge-SR mathematics and MinSR comparison

slides.title: Ridge SR: definitions
slides.footer: M counts retained configurations, not independent samples. P counts trainable parameters. These formulas use the real, positive-amplitude ansatz and fixed-N sector.

slides.title: Imaginary time and the metric
lines: SR matches a linearized variational step to imaginary-time evolution.
slides.footer: First-order wavefunction and second-order distance expansion; Monte Carlo estimates replace expectations. S is the real quantum geometric metric, not the energy Hessian.

slides.title: Ridge SR as least squares
lines: The code assigns d as the gradient to native SGD.
slides.footer: The Euclidean parameter penalty stabilizes ill-conditioned directions and changes the step. No Adam is applied after SR; the learning-rate convention absorbs the energy-gradient factor of two.

slides.title: The exact sample-space solve
lines: Same full batch and ridge; use the smaller dense system.
slides.footer: For positive tau, this is the same regularized direction in exact arithmetic. Centered sample rank is at most min(P,M−1). No additional sample, parameter or rank truncation is introduced.

slides.title: What ridge does to each mode
lines: Small-curvature directions are smoothly damped, not estimated reliably by assumption.
slides.footer: The ridge trades step fidelity for stability. A small sampled linearized step does not guarantee a small nonlinear wavefunction change or successful optimization.

slides.title: Relation to published MinSR
lines: Our ridge uses 1/(λ+τ); the optional comparison uses the published soft filter.
slides.footer: Chen & Heyl, Nature Physics 20, 1476–1481 (2024), doi:10.1038/s41567-024-02566-1, Methods Eqs.20–23. Zero modes require explicit handling; actual SGD update is −ηd.

slides.title: Cost, storage and precision
rows: Model derivatives may originate in float32
slides.footer: Costs exclude sampling and neural differentiation. Linear in P only at fixed M in the sample-space branch. Same-batch CPU audit: P=3681, M=256, primal/dual relative direction error 1.5×10⁻¹¹; not a long-run convergence proof.

slides.title: Comparison with the 1D routine
lines: $\tau=\lambda_{\rm sum}/M\quad\text{matches ridge units; centering still differs.}$
1D CPU code solves in float64; 2D solves on the training device in float64.
slides.footer: Changes to centering, ridge units and device are separate from Jacobian vectorization. The user accepted the 2D formulation. Gauge shifts can affect parameter differences without changing normalized-state tangents.
